chunks: And Abān ibn Taghlib narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:
Regarding a man who dies and has no heir and no mawla for him,
"He is among the people meant by this verse: 'They ask you about the anfal.'"

key_terms.الْآيَةِ: the Qur'anic verse cited as the basis of the ruling
key_terms.الْأَنْفَالِ: anfal; categories of property belonging to Allah and His Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and, in Shia understanding, under the authority of the Imam عليه السلام
key_terms.مَوْلًى: a patron or affiliated master who may hold a legal relationship to the deceased
key_terms.وَارِثَ: an heir entitled to inherit the deceased's estate
key_terms.يَسْأَلُونَكَ: they ask you; the opening word of the cited Qur'anic passage

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the wealth of someone who dies without heirs in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام places the estate of a person who dies without an heir or mawla under the ruling connected to the verse on al-anfāl. The narration indicates that such property belongs to the category of wealth governed by divine and Imam-authorized authority rather than private inheritance.
